heading: INT. BOOTH OF AN ABANDONED RADIO STATION - NIGHT

units.text: INT. BOOTH OF AN ABANDONED RADIO STATION - NIGHT
Dust.
Dead tubes.
A single working microphone on a bent boom arm, a red ON AIR light that flickers when it feels like it.
HORATIA KESSELRING-OLUMIDE (60s), a retired host with a voice like warm gravel, sits at the console in a green velvet jacket.
Good evening, listeners. If there are any of you left.
units.name: HORATIA

units.text: This is Horatia Kesselring, and this is the last broadcast of Midnight Confessional.
Tonight, we confess one thing.
Just one.
(beat)
Thirty-one years ago, a young man called this station from a phone booth on Delaney Street.
He said he had done something terrible.
He said he needed to tell somebody.
And I, in my infinite wisdom, said, "Call back tomorrow, honey.
We're out of time."
He never called back.
The next morning, police found a body on Delaney Street.
A girl.
Her name was Marian Pruitt.
(beat)
I kept the tape.
Every call, every night, thirty-one years.
I have never played this one for anyone.
Tonight I will.
She presses a key on the console.
Tape hiss.
Midnight Confessional, you're on the air.
units.name: HORATIA

units.text: Listen. That's me, at thirty. So bright. So certain.
units.name: HORATIA

units.text: Go ahead, caller. You're among friends.
units.name: HORATIA

units.text: He doesn't speak, you see. The tape is nineteen seconds of breathing. Nineteen. I counted them every night for thirty-one years.
units.name: HORATIA

units.text: (beat)
So I'll say what I should have said.
I'm sorry, Marian.
I'm sorry, whoever you were.
I should have stayed on the line.
(beat)
This has been Horatia Kesselring.
Good night, Delaney Street.
